title: Always-disabled buttons: enabled state renders disabled="" which still disables the control
evidence:
+            attribute("disabled", case busy {
+              True -> "disabled"
+              False -> ""
+            }),
...
+          attribute("disabled", case saving {
+            True -> "disabled"
+            False -> ""
+          }),
detail: Enabled state renders disabled="", an empty boolean attribute that still disables the control in HTML, so start-confirm Yes, take-over Yes, and edit-save buttons can never fire. Tests only assert the busy case renders disabled="disabled".
recommended_fix: Omit the attribute when not busy: build the attribute list conditionally (case busy { True -> [attribute("disabled", "disabled")]; False -> [] }) in all three spots.

title: Late-response guard claimed in comment but missing: stale ApiReturnedRefcheckAction toasts on any page
evidence:
+/// Fire a slot-scoped action (skip / re-enable / start). The slot comes
+/// from the row itself; the response rides `ApiReturnedRefcheckAction` with
+/// the call id + action name so a late answer after navigation is dropped
+/// by the id-match guard.
...
+    ApiReturnedRefcheckAction(call_id, action, result) ->
+      case result {
+        Ok(_) -> {
...
+          let #(m, toast_eff) = add_toast(cleared, toast_copy, ToastSuccess)
detail: Comment promises late answers are dropped by an id-match guard, but ApiReturnedRefcheckAction toasts on Ok and Error unconditionally; only the refetch is route-gated, so a stale response after navigation shows a toast on the wrong page.
recommended_fix: Guard the response handler: only toast/refetch when the call_id is still in refcheck_action_inflight (or the detail route is still active), matching the PDF-download pattern.

title: Immediate menu actions (skip/re-enable) fire without an inflight check — duplicate requests possible
evidence:
+        RefcheckSkip ->
+          fire_refcheck_slot_action(
+            menu_closed,
+            call_id,
+            "skip",
...
+        RefcheckReEnable ->
+          fire_refcheck_slot_action(
+            menu_closed,
+            call_id,
+            "re-enable",
detail: Unlike the confirm buttons (disabled while inflight), UserChoseRefcheckAction never checks refcheck_action_inflight, so reopening the menu mid-flight and clicking again double-fires; only the server's AD-14 pre-state guard rejects it.
recommended_fix: Drop the action (or disable menu entries) when the call_id is already in refcheck_action_inflight before firing.
